Original · Unique Research · 2026-05-22

Editor's note: The first-person report and its judgments belong to the original Chinese author. This English rendition retains the opening pull quote, all section headings, every percentage and demographic figure, and the closing TPEG model statement. Globalization, revenue, team-size, valuation and founder-age figures are source orself-reported data, not independently audited findings. The "5 billion" valuation threshold is preserved without an inferred currency. The award has run since 2023 per the source. Company, personal and work titles are transliterated where official English forms remain unverified.

Unique Awards · Shenzhen

2026 Global AI 100, Revealed

100 companies, right here.

"

Among this year's applicant companies, 25% derive more than half their revenue from overseas—up a full 10 percentage points from last year. 65% have overseas teams. This is not self-promotion; these are numbers filled into forms that can be verified. Globalization is shifting from a direction into a quantifiable outcome. 2026 Global AI 100, revealed today.

This Year Is Different from Last Year

We laid the application data from both years side by side, and several changes are worth noting.

Going global is no longer a label—it is a quantifiable result.

We included several directly numerical questions in the application form: the proportion of companies actually covering overseas markets, the share of overseas revenue, and the size of overseas teams. All three rose in 2026, and rose noticeably:

Companies actually operating in overseas markets grew from 41% to 55%. Those with more than half their revenue from overseas rose from 15% to 25%. Companies with overseas teams rose from 46% to 65%, and the ratio of overseas employees to total headcount rose from 9% to 14%.

Team size is the hardest indicator to fake. Hiring costs real money; managing people requires working across time zones. Behind these numbers is globalization that is actually happening—not a checkbox on an application form.

Industry applications have doubled.

Scenario applications and industry applications combined rose from 28% of total applicants last year to 44% this year. Correspondingly, horizontal "productivity tools" nearly halved.

The logic behind this shift is not complicated: the harder a position is to replace with a generic product, the more worth fighting for. Applicant companies are voting with their feet. They have collectively chosen tracks that are deeper, narrower, and harder to deliver results in—but once results are delivered, are very difficult to dislodge.

The leaders are accelerating into shape.

Companies valued at over 5 billion grew from less than 2% of the applicant pool to nearly 8% within one year. This is not to say the track is closed; rather, the first group to break out is running faster and faster, pulling away from those behind.

About This Year's Founders

One set of numbers left a strong impression on us.

Founders born in 1990 or later account for one-third of this year's applicant pool—up nearly 10 percentage points from last year. The youngest is 24.

But at the same time, the proportion of founders over 50 is also increasing. In the industry-application track, many are "veterans" who have spent two decades going deep in a specific vertical, re-entering the fray with real industry accumulation—AI is the new tool in their hands, and their industry is their old moat.

Both ends are stretching. This is the most interesting demographic structure in this year's applicant pool.

What Do 100 Companies Mean?

These 100 companies are not "China's best AI companies," nor are they "the AI companies that raised the most funding."

They are the ones in this cohort that have turned globalization into a real outcome—users overseas, revenue coming from overseas, teams rooted in their target markets.

We have run this award since 2023, and every year we look at the same thing: AI is the foundation, globalization is the result. Accomplishing both at once is harder than accomplishing either one alone.

The 100 companies on stage today have done it.

We will continue to track them.

2026 Global AI 100 is comprehensively assessed by the TPEG four-dimensional model (Technology leadership, Product competitiveness, Commercial growth, Globalization progress)
